description: Verify two scientific claims against real abstracts (support+NEI); one paper is unrelated. Cite the evidence for each verdict.
task_prompt:
Two claims are under review.
Claim 1: ATM and Rad3 related protein have no role in sensing DNA damage.
Claim 2: Osteocytes have an essential role in G-CSF induced HSPC mobilization.
Using the papers in documents/, decide for each claim whether the evidence supports it, contradicts it, or does not give enough information to decide. Write each verdict on its own line as 'Claim N: SUPPORTED', 'Claim N: CONTRADICTED' or 'Claim N: NOT ENOUGH INFO'. For each verdict, cite the paper and the specific result behind it.

seeds.text: ATM and Rad3 related protein have no role in sensing DNA damage.
Osteocytes have an essential role in G-CSF induced HSPC mobilization.
rationale: Granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF), used clinically to mobilize HSPCs, induces changes in the morphology and gene expression of the osteocytic network that precedes changes in osteoblasts.
Mice with targeted ablation of osteocytes or a disrupted osteocyte network have comparable numbers of HSPCs in the BM but fail to mobilize HSPCs in response to G-CSF.

claim_1_verdict.description: Claim 1 is not enough info by the evidence
keywords: not enough information to evaluate claim 1
claim_1_verdict.claim: ATM and Rad3 related protein have no role in sensing DNA damage.

claim_2_verdict.description: Claim 2 is supported by the evidence
claim_2_verdict.claim: Osteocytes have an essential role in G-CSF induced HSPC mobilization.

claim_1_called_support.description: Claim 1 called supported, but the truth is not enough info

claim_1_called_contradict.description: Claim 1 called contradicted, but the truth is not enough info

claim_2_called_contradict.description: Claim 2 called contradicted, but the truth is supported

tool_result.alt_conclusion: Taken together, these results contradict the claim that osteocytes have an essential role in G-CSF induced HSPC mobilization.

key_findings.value: Verified: Paper B contradicts Claim 2 (Osteocytes have an essential role in G-CSF induced HSPC mobilization.)
